rv.q: An evening of laughter, song and dance is the right track to mend.
But for all that, somewhere between the screen and the stage, something in “Groundhog Day: The Musical” has been lost in translation.
From the marvelous, man-sized marmot to The Marching Chucks , you won’t need a wake-up call to fall in love all over again with Paramount’s “Groundhog Day.”
And now "Groundhog Day" is a musical, which in the Paramount Theatre’s lively, funny, sometimes darkly comic, tuneful, cleverly staged production, the story touches all those notes.
With a production and acting of the quality you would find in the “big city,” this show about small town America, do-overs and redemption warmed my heart on this snowy night.
Indeed, ‘GroundHog Day: The Musical,’ is a tremendous musical production.
It’s just that the repetitious storyline, which begins as humorous, eventually wears thin and becomes simply annoying.
The choreography (Megan E. Farley) and Musical Direction ( Kory Danielson) are sheer perfection as we have learned to expect at the Paramount Theatre.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this musical adaptation, with praise for its production values and lead performance but criticism that the repetitive book and forgettable score fail to capture the beloved film's charm.
